steps.narration: Responsive Areas. Different area layouts for every screen size, in the Umbraco Block Grid.
Here is a block with four areas: A, B, C and D.
As the screen narrows, the areas change size and order. It's all set up in the backoffice. Let's see how.
Open the block in your Block Grid data type, and go to the Areas tab.
Grid Columns for Areas sets the grid. Here, twelve, filled in from the data type.
The first layout has no breakpoint. Add your areas here. It's used on every screen, unless a layout below applies.
Then add a layout for each breakpoint. Each one has a breakpoint alias, here large, medium and small, and its own grid columns. Every layout uses the same areas.
Drag a box to change its order. Drag its corner to change its size.
On the page, each area gets CSS variables. The breakpoint alias is on the end of each name. The values are the spans and order from the backoffice.
Your own CSS decides when each breakpoint applies. This site uses Bootstrap, so the medium layout uses Bootstrap's medium width.
The same variables work just as well with Tailwind, Foundation, or your own CSS. Only the breakpoint rule changes.
Let's change something. In the medium layout, area B is three columns wide. Drag its corner to six. Submit, and save.
One value changes. B's column span at medium goes from three to six.
Refresh at tablet width. B now spans the full width.
Now the small layout. Drag D to the front, and save.
The order values update. D is now first.
On a phone, D now comes first. Order changes what you see. The reading order stays the same as the first layout.
Responsive Areas. Set up in the backoffice, styled with your own CSS. Your areas are stored the standard Umbraco way, so your blocks keep working if you remove it.
